name: Pythagorean Triple (Euclid): Leg a
description: Gives the odd leg m² − n² of the Pythagorean triple generated by Euclid's formula from integers m > n > 0.
notes: The triple is primitive when m and n are coprime and not both odd; m = 5, n = 2 gives (21, 20, 29).

name: Pythagorean Triple (Euclid): Leg b
description: Gives the even leg 2mn of the Pythagorean triple from Euclid's formula.
notes: Every primitive triple has exactly one even leg, and it is divisible by 4.

name: Pythagorean Triple (Euclid): Hypotenuse c
description: Gives the hypotenuse m² + n² of the Pythagorean triple from Euclid's formula.

name: Pythagorean Triple Test
description: Returns 1 when a² + b² = c² exactly.
notes: Integer triples such as (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13) and (20, 21, 29) satisfy it.

name: Primitive Pythagorean Triples up to Hypotenuse N (Estimate)
description: Estimates the number of primitive Pythagorean triples with hypotenuse at most N as N/(2π) (Lehmer 1900).
notes: The exact count up to 1000 is 158, against the estimate 159.2.

name: Primitive Pythagorean Triples up to Hypotenuse N (Exact)
expression: sum(m, 2, isqrt(n), sum(k, 1, m - 1, and(and(gcd(m, k) == 1, mod(m - k, 2) == 1), m^2 + k^2 <= n)))
description: Counts the primitive Pythagorean triples with hypotenuse at most N by running through Euclid's parameters m > k (coprime, opposite parity).
notes: There are 158 with hypotenuse up to 1000.

name: Linear Diophantine Equation Solvability
description: Returns 1 when ax + by = c has integer solutions, which happens exactly when gcd(a, b) divides c.
notes: 12x + 42y = 30 is solvable (gcd 6 divides 30), e.g. x = −1, y = 1.

name: Linear Diophantine Equation: Smallest Non-negative x
expression: mod(c / gcd(a, b) * if(b / gcd(a, b) == 1, 0, modinv(a / gcd(a, b), b / gcd(a, b))), b / gcd(a, b))
description: Solves ax + by = c for the smallest x ≥ 0 (y then follows as (c − ax)/b); all solutions are x + k·b/g.
notes: Requires gcd(a, b) to divide c. For 12x + 42y = 30: x = 6, y = −1.

name: Number of Non-negative Solutions of ax + by = n
expression: sum(x, 0, n / a, mod(n - a * x, b) == 0)
description: Counts the pairs of non-negative integers (x, y) with ax + by = n, e.g. the ways to pay n with coins a and b.
notes: 100 can be made from 3s and 5s in 7 ways.

name: Pell Equation Solution x_k (x² − Dy² = 1)
description: Generates the k-th solution x_k of Pell's equation x² − Dy² = 1 from the fundamental solution (x₁, y₁), via x_k + y_k√D = (x₁ + y₁√D)^k.
notes: For D = 2 from (3, 2): x₅ = 3363 (and y₅ = 2378). Exact while the numbers stay below about 10^15.

name: Pell Equation Solution y_k (x² − Dy² = 1)
expression: round(((x1 + y1 * sqrt(d))^k - (x1 - y1 * sqrt(d))^k) / (2 * sqrt(d)))
description: Generates the y-part of the k-th solution of Pell's equation from the fundamental solution.
notes: x_k/y_k are excellent rational approximations to √D: 3363/2378 ≈ 1.41421356.

name: Pell Equation Check x² − Dy²
description: Evaluates x² − Dy². A result of 1 confirms a solution of Pell's equation.
notes: (649, 180) is the fundamental solution for D = 13.

name: Brahmagupta's Identity (Product of Sums of Two Squares)
description: Writes (a² + b²)(c² + d²) as a single sum of two squares: (ac − bd)² + (ad + bc)².
notes: Shows that products of sums of two squares are again sums of two squares: 5 × 13 = 65 = 4² + 7².

name: Sum of Two Cubes
description: Computes a³ + b³.
notes: 1729 = 12³ + 1³ = 10³ + 9³ is the smallest number expressible as a sum of two cubes in two ways (the taxicab number).

name: Taxicab Representation Count
expression: sum(a, 1, cbrt(n), sum(b, a, cbrt(n), a^3 + b^3 == n))
description: Counts the ways to write n as a³ + b³ with 1 ≤ a ≤ b.
notes: 1729 has two representations; 87,539,319 is the smallest number with three.

name: Egyptian Fraction: Greedy First Unit Fraction
description: Gives the denominator of the largest unit fraction 1/k not exceeding n/d — the first step of Fibonacci's greedy algorithm for Egyptian fractions.

name: Egyptian Fraction: Remainder after the Greedy Step
description: Gives what is left of n/d after subtracting the greedy unit fraction 1/⌈d/n⌉. Its numerator is always smaller than n, so the method ends.
notes: For 4/13 the remainder is 3/52 ≈ 0.057692.

name: Mediant of Two Fractions
description: Computes the mediant (a + c)/(b + d) of a/b and c/d, which always lies between them.
notes: Mediants build the Stern–Brocot tree and Farey sequences: between 1/3 and 1/2 lies 2/5.

name: Farey Neighbour Test
description: Returns 1 when |bc − ad| = 1, the condition for a/b and c/d to be neighbours in some Farey sequence.
notes: 2/5 and 1/2 are neighbours: 5·1 − 2·2 = 1.

name: Ford Circle Radius
description: Gives the radius of the Ford circle of a reduced fraction p/q: the circle tangent to the number line at p/q.
notes: Ford circles of Farey neighbours touch but never overlap.

name: Continued Fraction Convergent Error Bound
description: Bounds how close a continued-fraction convergent pₙ/qₙ is to x: |x − pₙ/qₙ| < 1/(qₙ qₙ₊₁).
notes: For π ≈ 355/113 the next denominator is 33,102, so the error is below 2.7 × 10⁻⁷ (it is actually 2.67 × 10⁻⁷).

name: Hurwitz Approximation Bound
description: Hurwitz's theorem: every irrational x has infinitely many fractions p/q with |x − p/q| < 1/(√5 q²); √5 cannot be improved (because of the golden ratio).
notes: For q = 113 the bound is about 3.5 × 10⁻⁵; 355/113 beats it by far.

name: Continued Fraction [a0; a1, a2, a3]
description: Evaluates the finite continued fraction a₀ + 1/(a₁ + 1/(a₂ + 1/a₃)).
notes: [3; 7, 15, 1] = 355/113 ≈ 3.1415929204, the famous approximation of π by Zu Chongzhi.
